# TLS certificate verification disabled (C#)

`qualor:csharp/tls-verification-disabled` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-295](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/295.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A07:2025 Authentication Failures](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A07_2025-Authentication_Failures/), [A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A07_2021-Identification_and_Authentication_Failures/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Certificate validation that is switched off in .NET clients:

- a lambda, anonymous method or method that returns `true` whatever it is given, used as the validation callback of `HttpClientHandler` or `SocketsHttpHandler` (`ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback`, `SslOptions.RemoteCertificateValidationCallback`), of `ServicePointManager.ServerCertificateValidationCallback`, of `SslClientAuthenticationOptions` or `ClientWebSocketOptions` (`RemoteCertificateValidationCallback`), or passed to `new SslStream(...)` or `new RemoteCertificateValidationCallback(...)`;
- a method with an `SslPolicyErrors` parameter whose body only returns `true` (reported at the method);
- `HttpClientHandler.DangerousAcceptAnyServerCertificateValidator`.

Callbacks that look at `sslPolicyErrors`, compare a pinned thumbprint, return `false` or throw on a problem are not reported. Test code is skipped.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Without certificate validation the client cannot tell the real server from anyone else on the network path. An attacker who can intercept the connection (public Wi-Fi, a compromised router, a hostile proxy) presents any certificate, reads credentials and data, and changes responses, and the application notices nothing. Code written "just for development" often reaches production.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the handler trusts every server certificate.

```csharp
using System.Net.Http;

public class ApiClient
{
    public HttpClient Create()
    {
        var handler = new HttpClientHandler();
        handler.ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback = (message, cert, chain, errors) => true;
        return new HttpClient(handler);
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the default validation is kept.

```csharp
using System.Net.Http;

public class ApiClient
{
    public HttpClient Create()
    {
        return new HttpClient(new HttpClientHandler());
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Remove the callback: the platform validates the chain and the host name.
- If you need a custom check, return `errors == SslPolicyErrors.None`, or add a check on top (a pinned thumbprint, your own private CA added to `X509Chain.ChainPolicy.CustomTrustStore`) and still return `false` when anything is wrong.
- For a development server, trust its certificate on the machine (`dotnet dev-certs https --trust`) instead of disabling validation.
- Never ship `DangerousAcceptAnyServerCertificateValidator`; it is meant for tests.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- HttpClient (System.Net.Http)
- SslStream
- `servicepointmanager`

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A lambda is checked where it is given directly to one of the properties or constructors above. A callback kept in a variable first is missed.
- A method is reported where it is declared, not where it is used; a method that returns `true` after a check that neither returns nor throws (a log line, an `if` that only logs) is reported too.
- A block-bodied callback counts as accepting everything only when it returns `true` and has no other `return` and no `throw`. Callbacks that accept only some errors (a host name mismatch, say) are not reported.
- A callback that is only installed under a condition (a development flag) is still reported.
- Code in a file OpenGrep cannot parse (some C# 11 and 12 syntax: `$$"""` raw strings, `class X : Y;`, some multi-line collection expressions) is not checked.
- Files under `test/`, `tests/`, `*.Tests/`, `*.UnitTests/`, `*.IntegrationTests/`, `*.Test/` and `*.Specs/` and named `*Tests.cs` or `*Test.cs` are skipped.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/csharp/tls/tls-verification-disabled.cs`](../../../rules/csharp/tls/tls-verification-disabled.cs) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/csharp/tls/tls-verification-disabled.yml`](../../../rules/csharp/tls/tls-verification-disabled.yml), added in version 2026.10.5.
